facts_and_constraints: R/S labels describe the chiral 1-phenylethyl substituents used in synthesis, not a supplied backbone assignment.
The fused dimer and monomer have different stoichiometries and connections. Differences in their total electronic energies are not optical transition energies or a balanced association energy.

Experimental optical observations and ancillary chromatography/NMR conditions are provided in solution_observations.json. No measured conformer free energies or calibrated molecular spectral tolerance is supplied.
identity_provenance: Main Figure1a and SI synthesis/full-side-chain coordinate records establish chlorinated PDI monomer and fused-dimer connections with 1-phenylethyl R/S substituents. These mapped molecular graphs preserve the substituent stereocentres but provide no optimized geometry, backbone helicity or conformer weights.
decisions_open: Choose relevant molecular configurations and any defensible representation or population treatment.
Choose how to explain the absorption/CD changes and evidence that could refute or revise that explanation.
Decide which structural or environmental uncertainties affect the inferred chiroptical response and whether existing observations resolve them.
removed_v1_requirements: Remove fixed M-family backbone, specified side-chain ensemble size and prescribed cut/cap coupling control.
Remove mandatory mirror-calibration job and nominated transition/dipole mechanism from AR inputs and active requirements.
Keep the known side-chain absolute configurations and real solution observations; release backbone assignments rather than deleting necessary experimental facts.
out_of_scope: Study the four supplied complete neutral singlet molecular identities and their molecular optical response in dichloromethane. Side-chain stereochemistry is a known synthetic identity; backbone helicity, relevant conformations, populations and transition assignments are to be investigated. The supplied graphs do not prescribe a three-dimensional backbone. Ancillary HPLC/NMR observations retain their own experimental media and do not establish a dichloromethane equilibrium distribution. A reduced model requires an explicit relationship to the full molecular identity and a justification adequate for its claim. Periodic crystals, charge transport, photocurrent dissymmetry and device efficiency are outside the required molecular question.
feasibility: The source explicitly carries out molecular ORCA optimization, single-point and TDDFT-CD computations for the full systems. Complete source-connected graphs are available here, so input identity is not blocked. Future reference review can first reparse existing full-side-chain inputs and TD outputs where actually available; then assess the chosen molecular route. The 138-atom dimer requires a realistic runtime allocation, which has not been measured for V2. Any reduced model must demonstrate its relevance rather than inherit validity from size reduction.
limitations: Only summarized measured spectra and ancillary observations are public; no false pointwise raw spectrum or error bar is supplied. Full solution conformational/population and alternate-route optical references remain pending. Source crystal configuration does not establish the solution ensemble. Semantic judge calibration, independent scientific validation and filesystem isolation remain pending.
review_type: Local relevant primary-text/figure review with explicit page mapping; no new scientific calculation.
